topics.topic: What format and entropy requirements apply to owner-session identities
questions: Is an owner-session identity a UUID, or an opaque value containing at least 32 random bytes?

quotes: Minting every opaque identity Registry makes — `project_id`, `room_id`, pointer id, `customer_ref`, the owner session's identity, the confirmation id — as a random UUID ("Identity formats"); making the 32-byte values of A13 rule 7 from the operating system's random source; comparing a presented secret with a held one in constant time (A13 rule 7, A17 rule 6).

The session's identity, its CSRF value and a confirmation value are each at least 32 bytes from the operating system's random source; each is compared in constant time and never appears in a URL, a log line, a diagnostic or an audit entry (R0-29, R0-37).

quotes: Every action is one call of `operations` and, when it changes state, one store transaction (A04 rule 4): `operations` opens it through `store.run_in_transaction`, calls each module the action changes inside it, appends the action's one audit entry through `audit_log.append_audit_entry` when the action changed state (A14 rule 1) and commits once.
An entry is written by an accepted action that changes state and that M09 lists, in the same transaction as the change: if the change is not stored, neither is the entry, and the reverse.
judgement.why: State 3 says every changed action receives an audit entry, while A14 restricts entries to changed actions listed by M09.

questions: Is the set of service-token configuration items derived from the release's service table, or is it a separate fixed list owned by `configuration`; if derived, how may `configuration` know `release_declarations`?

quotes: What a release declares and a running instance reads from it alone: A22 — the artifact types with their owner services, the first release's one type (`estimate`, PresuPro) — A09 rule 2's table of the services, their operations and their highest classes;

A17: reading the `REGISTRY_` environment variables and nothing else; the start checks in rule 2's one order — no unknown item, the service tokens all four or none, the other items present, each well formed, each secret at least 32 bytes, no two secrets equal — with the diagnostic naming the failed item and never its value; that no default is applied (rule 5); an owner-only start when no token is given (rule 1).
`models`.
A new service, or a change of a row, enters by a specification change and a release (R0-27, R0-33).
judgement.divergence: After a release declares a fifth service, `configuration` either continues enforcing its independent four-token roster and rejects the new token as unknown, or derives the roster from `release_declarations` and accepts all five; the owner and new service notice whether Registry starts.
judgement.why: The service roster is owned by `release_declarations`, but `configuration` enforces a fixed roster while being forbidden by its dependency list from knowing `release_declarations`.
